tasks.title: C++ Book (PPP) — ch 1-10 core; 17-21 may carry
Ray tracer README with progressive renders

focus.item: Programming: Principles and Practice Using C++
focus.desc: Pointers, references, manual memory allocation, and STL containers. Prioritise ch 8-10 — the ray tracer depends on them; ch 17-21 may carry into Phase 2.
Vector spaces, matrix multiplication, transforms, and the local/world/view/projection coordinate chain.
Canvas, ray casting, shading, sphere intersections, shadows, reflection and refraction.
Window setup, coordinate systems, and the first rendering shaders. Completed in Phase 2.
Public ray-tracer repo with progressive renders embedded in the README — flat circle, shaded sphere, full reflective scene.

math.desc: Vector and matrix math, and coordinate spaces (local, world, view, projection).

algoDS.desc: Array of Structures (AoS) vs. Structure of Arrays (SoA), memory alignment and padding, and fixed-size pools to avoid heap overhead.
Pattern templates: Two Pointers, Sliding Window, Hash Maps, Stack/Monotonic Stack, Advanced Binary Search.

deliverable.desc: A standalone CPU-bound C++ renderer shading spheres with shadows and reflections, shipped with a visual README.

tasks.title: Scene graph with iterative DFS/BFS traversal

focus.desc: Core profile, GLSL, texturing, Blinn-Phong lighting, Assimp model loading, framebuffers, cubemaps, instancing, shadow mapping and normal mapping.
Templates, RAII, STL algorithms and lambdas — applied immediately as RAII wrappers around OpenGL buffer, texture and shader handles.
Live controls for light positions, material colours, shader and texture switching, and camera FOV.
Inspect bound pipelines and uniforms, step through shader variables. Target skill: diagnose a black screen from the capture alone.
Wireframe vectors, coordinate axes, and bounding boxes in world space. Relied on heavily in Phase 3.
Screen-captured demo video plus README stills showing a lit, shadowed model with the ImGui panel visible.

math.desc: Differentiation rules and the chain rule.
Derive the tangent/bitangent frame for normal mapping from partial derivatives of position with respect to UV — by hand, before using LearnOpenGL's code.
Fitting a shadow map frustum tightly to a scene is a constrained min/max optimization problem.

algoDS.desc: A tree of nodes propagating transforms parent-to-child. Built here because the viewer needs it; promoted to an engine subsystem in Phase 3.
Depth-first and breadth-first traversal with an explicit stack rather than recursion, so deep hierarchies cannot blow the call stack mid-frame.
Heap/Priority Queue, Trees/DFS/BFS, Interval Problems, DP Basics. Do the tree patterns in the same weeks as the scene graph — same skill.

deliverable.desc: A real-time 3D renderer loading meshes via Assimp, with a scene graph, free-fly camera, Blinn-Phong lighting, shadow mapping and an ImGui control panel.

tasks.title: Arena + pool allocator, with before/after measurements
SQLite asset database + offline bake step
Implement BVH from scratch + frustum culling
Post-processing: SSAO, bloom, HDR tone mapping

focus.desc: Where the artifact stops being a renderer and starts being an engine.
Ch 5 subsystem lifecycles and the main loop, ch 7 arena/stack/pool allocators, ch 14 the render subsystem.
Replace new/delete in the mesh and texture load paths with an arena plus a pool allocator. Measure load time and peak allocation count before and after. No measurement means the chapter is not done.
Read only the chapters whose techniques already exist in your renderer — shading equations, shadow algorithms, environment mapping. It is a derivation reference, not a tutorial.

SQLite as an offline, editor-side asset database — materials, meshes and textures plus a join table for mesh-material reuse. Compare a relational adjacency list against nested JSON for the scene hierarchy. A bake step emits a flat binary; the runtime loads that and never opens the database.
Make it fast, and prove it with numbers.
G-buffer layout and decoupling the light pass from geometry. An architectural rewrite of the render path, not a feature — budget accordingly.
SSAO, bloom, HDR tone mapping, and cascaded or perspective shadow maps.
CPU/GPU frame boundary tracking, plus ImGui toggles for BVH and frustum culling overlays with live culled-geometry counts.
Pipe captures into SQLite (frame number, CPU time, GPU time, draw calls) and write real aggregates — slowest frames, average by scene, percentiles.

A written performance case study: before/after frame times, what the profiler showed, what changed, what it bought. The numbers come straight out of the frame-timing database. The single most valuable artifact in the plan for hiring.

math.desc: Integration techniques, numerical approximation, and infinite series. Applied to physics integration loops (Euler and Verlet).
Partial derivatives and gradients started here on purpose, so Phase 4 is not learning Vulkan and multivariable calculus at the same time.

algoDS.desc: Bounding volume hierarchies (BVH) over axis-aligned bounding boxes (AABBs), plus quadtrees and octrees for view culling.
Build it in the engine and drive view frustum culling with it. Verify culled-geometry counts using the Phase 2 debug drawer.
Graphs & Advanced DP: topological sort, union-find, 2D DP on grids and strings. Continue medium/hard practice across all earlier patterns.

deliverable.desc: The scene viewer promoted to an engine: subsystem lifecycle, custom allocators, a baked asset pipeline, deferred rendering, BVH frustum culling, post-processing, and a profiler-backed performance case study.

tasks.title: Diagnose Vulkan queues & pipeline state in RenderDoc
Radix/merge sort for transparent depth sorting
OpenGL vs Vulkan writeup + full portfolio pass

focus.desc: Scope matches what two months can actually produce: a correct, explicit, textured mesh renderer. PBR and IBL are not in this phase.
Instances, validation layers, physical and logical devices, swapchains, render passes, framebuffers and command pools.
Graphics pipelines, descriptor sets, push constants, vertex/index and staging buffers, device memory allocation, texture images, image views, samplers and depth buffering.
Semaphores, fences, and pipeline barriers — the part that actually decides whether a Vulkan renderer is correct.
Analyse memory allocations, verify descriptor layouts, debug image layout transitions, and inspect device queues.
A written OpenGL-vs-Vulkan comparison, plus a full portfolio pass: three repos, each with a README, media, and a clear statement of what it demonstrates.

math.desc: Double and triple integrals, gradients, curl and divergence. Begun in Phase 3 so it is not competing with Vulkan here.
Random variables, expectation, variance, estimator bias and importance sampling. Previously missing from the plan entirely — nothing in physically based rendering makes sense without it.
Derived and understood here, using the integration and probability above. Implemented later — see Beyond the Horizon.

algoDS.desc: Half-edge structure for polygon mesh adjacency queries. Implemented index-based and in-memory — the point is cache-coherent traversal, so it is deliberately not modelled in a database.
Radix or merge sort for depth-sorting transparent geometry back-to-front every frame.
Sorting algorithm mechanics and advanced graph problems on adjacency lists.
Trie, Backtracking, Advanced Graphs: Word Search II, Design Add/Search Words, advanced traversal. Full pattern review at hard difficulty.

deliverable.desc: An explicit Vulkan renderer setting up its own pipelines, descriptor sets and device buffers to draw textured meshes with correct synchronization.
